chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abbad ibn Shu'ayb, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never bivouacked (made a night encampment for battle) against an enemy.'

key_terms.بَيَّتَ: To bivouack or make a night encampment for battle

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do regarding night encampments against enemies?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not conduct night encampments (*bayt*) against enemies, distinguishing his practice from the broader concept of night raids (*ghazawat*). This highlights the Prophet's preference for strategic clarity and avoiding the confusion of night battles, a nuance often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding military etiquette. The statement serves to refine the understanding of prophetic military conduct by specifying the type of engagement excluded.
